categories.title: Discipline & Orders
categories.subtitle: Maintain discipline, respect the chain of command, and follow lawful orders.
previewBullets: Following lawful orders promptly and without hesitation
Respecting established military chain of command
Military courtesy, salutes and professional discipline
Personal responsibility, accountability and duty integrity

rules.title: Following Lawful Orders
rules.explanation: All military personnel are legally bound to obey all lawful commands issued by their appointed military superiors promptly, respectfully, and without dispute.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — Section 41 (Disobedience to superior officer)
rules.details: Failure to obey a lawful command given by a superior officer in the execution of his office constitutes a court-martial offence under military law.

rules.title: Respecting the Chain of Command
rules.explanation: All communications, operational reports, representations, and administrative applications must strictly follow the established line of command through Section, Platoon, and Company commanders.
rules.reference: Regulations for the Army (Revised Edition) — Para 421
rules.details: Bypassing the chain of command to communicate with higher headquarters or external authorities is strictly prohibited.

rules.title: Military Courtesy & Professional Bearing
rules.explanation: Proper military compliments, salutes, and formal address by rank must be rendered to all superior officers, commissioned ranks, and national colours at all times.
rules.reference: Regulations for the Army — Para 435 (Compliments & Salutes)
rules.details: Courtesy reinforces command cohesion and unit morale. Compliments must be exchanged smartly and reciprocated by seniors.

rules.title: Personal Responsibility & Accountability
rules.explanation: Every serviceman bears direct personal accountability for their conduct, arms, ammunition, and assigned post duties during peace, training, and operational conditions.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — General Principles of Military Discipline
rules.details: An individual cannot delegate personal responsibility for vigilance or safety on guard duty.

categories.title: Uniform & Appearance
categories.subtitle: Maintain required dress standards, grooming, and military courtesy.
previewBullets: Observance of authorized pattern uniforms and badges of rank
Strict grooming, haircut, and personal hygiene standards
Dress regulations in public areas and prohibition of civilian mixing

rules.title: Applicable Uniform Standards
rules.explanation: Personnel must wear only authorized pattern combat dress, service dress, or ceremonial uniform with official badges of rank, ribbons, and regimental accoutrements.
rules.reference: Dress Regulations for the Army (Revised 2022)
rules.details: Non-regulation modifications, unauthorized badges, or altered camouflage patterns are strictly prohibited on duty and parade.

rules.title: Grooming & Military Bearing
rules.explanation: Haircuts must be neatly trimmed above the collar, beards regulated according to regimental authorization, and personal bearing must reflect military pride.
rules.reference: Regulations for the Army — Grooming & Bearing Directives
rules.details: Soldiers on active strength must present a clean-shaven or regimentally authorized appearance at morning muster rolls.

rules.title: Observing Dress Regulations in Public
rules.explanation: Uniform must never be mixed with civilian clothing, worn in disreputable public venues, or worn while travelling without formal authorization orders.
rules.reference: Army Orders (Dress & Public Decorum Standards)
rules.details: Wearing partial uniform items (e.g. combat jacket with civilian jeans) undermines service dignity and is prohibited.

categories.title: Attendance & Punctuality
categories.subtitle: Report on time, follow muster roll procedures, and adhere to leave authorizations.
previewBullets: Reporting on time for muster rolls, guard mounting, and assigned shifts
Adherence to duty roster check-in and relief handover procedures
Understanding authorized leave sanctions and reporting timelines

rules.title: Punctuality & Parade Fall-In
rules.explanation: All personnel must report at least 10 minutes prior to scheduled parades, roll calls, and duty shift handovers. Unexplained absence is strictly punishable.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — Section 39 (Absence without leave)
rules.details: Absence from appointed place of parade or duty without sufficient cause is subject to summary military trial.

rules.title: Duty Roster Attendance Protocol
rules.explanation: Soldiers assigned to perimeter checkposts, main gate sentry, or QRT standby must remain present at their station until formally relieved by the relief guard.
rules.reference: Base Standing Orders — Guard Mounting & Post Manning
rules.details: Abandoning a guard post or falling asleep on sentry duty constitutes a severe breach of the Army Act.

rules.title: Authorized Leave & Reporting Requirements
rules.explanation: Leave must be sanctioned through Part II Orders. Soldiers must report back to their unit before expiry of leave, and immediately report their arrival at the Guard Room.
rules.reference: Army Leave Rules & Regulations for the Army Para 472
rules.details: Overstaying leave requires immediate communication with the unit Adjutant along with government hospital medical certificates if hospitalized.

categories.title: Code of Conduct
categories.subtitle: Honesty and integrity, respectful behaviour, and professional conduct on and off duty.
previewBullets: Unflinching honesty, moral integrity, and truthful reporting
Respectful behaviour, dignity, and comradeship across all ranks
Strict zero tolerance for harassment, ragging, or discrimination
Exemplary professional conduct on duty and in civilian interactions

rules.title: Honesty & Moral Integrity
rules.explanation: Complete truthfulness in official logbooks, reports, and administrative rolls is expected. Falsification of documents is severely penalised under military law.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — Section 45 (Unbecoming conduct) & Section 57
rules.details: Making false official statements or fraudulent entries in military records undermines base security.

rules.title: Respectful Behaviour & Comradeship
rules.explanation: Mutual trust, respect, and cohesive camaraderie form the operational foundation of armed combat units. Bullying or derogatory language is unacceptable.
rules.reference: Military Ethos & Regimental Code of the Indian Army
rules.details: Officers and JCOs must lead by personal example, ensuring welfare and equitable treatment of all personnel under their command.

rules.title: Zero Tolerance for Harassment & Discrimination
rules.explanation: The Indian Army strictly prohibits any form of ragging, hazing, harassment, or discrimination based on caste, creed, religion, or regional origin.
rules.reference: Equal Opportunity & Anti-Ragging Directives (Army HQ)
rules.details: Violators are liable to immediate disciplinary action and removal from service.

rules.title: Professional Conduct On and Off Duty
rules.explanation: Personnel represent the nation and the Indian Army at all times. They must maintain sobriety, avoid public debt disputes, and respect civil laws.
rules.reference: Regulations for the Army — Para 428 (Civil Conduct & Decorum)
rules.details: Intoxication while on duty or disorderly conduct in civilian areas results in swift court-martial action.

categories.title: Confidentiality & Security
categories.subtitle: Protect sensitive information, credentials, official records, and restricted material.
previewBullets: Protection of operational plans, roster records, and classified data
Securing military portal accounts, login credentials, and digital keys
Compliance with photography, smartphone, and social media bans
Immediate counter-intelligence reporting of unauthorized disclosures

rules.title: Protecting Sensitive & Classified Information
rules.explanation: Details of military unit dispositions, duty assignments, ammunition holdings, and patrol timings are strictly confidential and must never be discussed with unauthorized persons.
rules.reference: Official Secrets Act, 1923 & Army Security Regulations
rules.details: Classified documents must be handled strictly on a 'Need to Know' basis and stored in double-locked security safes.

rules.title: Digital Accounts & Credential Security
rules.explanation: User accounts, passwords, and cryptographic keys used for accessing base command systems and duty portals must never be shared or written in unsecured places.
rules.reference: Cyber Security Directives for Armed Forces (CERT-Army)
rules.details: Sharing login credentials or inserting unauthorized USB storage media into military workstations is a punishable breach.

rules.title: Social Media & Photography Restrictions
rules.explanation: Taking photographs inside military installations, posting in uniform on social media, or revealing troop locations online is strictly banned.
rules.reference: Army Cyber Security Policy & Social Media Guidelines (Revised)
rules.details: Smartphone usage is restricted in operational offices, armouries, and command war rooms.

rules.title: Counter-Intelligence Reporting
rules.explanation: Any suspicious inquiry, honey-trap approach, or unauthorized request for military information must be reported immediately to the Military Intelligence (MI) cell.
rules.reference: Standing Counter-Intelligence Orders
rules.details: Failure to report suspected espionage or hostile intelligence overtures constitutes complicity under the Army Act.

categories.title: Equipment & Property
categories.subtitle: Responsible use of authorized equipment, custody recordkeeping, and discrepancy reporting.
previewBullets: Responsible handling of weapons, ammunition, optics, and gear
Strict compliance with armoury storage and cleaning procedures
Immediate reporting of damaged, defective, or missing property
Maintaining continuous and verified custody ledger records

rules.title: Responsible Use of Authorized Equipment
rules.explanation: Government-issued weapons, tactical optics, wireless sets, and transport vehicles must be operated strictly for official duty and maintained in combat-ready state.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — Section 54 (Deficiency of equipment)
rules.details: Negligent loss or damage to government equipment incurs disciplinary action and financial recovery.

rules.title: Armoury Storage & Safety Clearing
rules.explanation: Firearms must be physically cleared at the safety sand-bucket before entry into the kote/armoury and deposited immediately upon conclusion of the duty shift.
rules.reference: Standard Operating Procedures for Unit Armouries (Kote SOP)
rules.details: Weapons must be locked in designated unit racks under the joint supervision of the Unit Armourer and Havaldar Major.

rules.title: Reporting Missing or Damaged Property
rules.explanation: Any defect, cracked optic, weapon malfunction, or missing equipment item must be reported immediately to the Quartermaster for formal recording.
rules.reference: Equipment Management Guidelines (EMG)
rules.details: Concealing a weapon defect or loss is an offence. Immediate reporting enables formal replacement and technical investigation.

rules.title: Accurate Custody Ledger Maintenance
rules.explanation: Every weapon issuance, ammunition box draw, and night vision handover must be documented with signatures in physical registers and digital DDMS records.
rules.reference: Materiel Management & Ordnance Audit Regulations
rules.details: Discrepancies in serial numbers between ledger and physical firearm must be reconciled before daily armoury closing.

categories.title: Safety & Training
categories.subtitle: Approved safety procedures, combat training drills, and health/fitness standards.
previewBullets: Adherence to firing range protocols and live ammunition safety
Mandatory attendance at scheduled tactical refreshers and drills
Immediate reporting of physical hazards, fire risks, and incidents
Maintaining requisite SHAPE-1 medical classification and fitness

rules.title: Firing Range & Ammunition Safety
rules.explanation: Strict range discipline is compulsory. Weapons must point down-range at all times, with safety catches engaged until the command 'Fire' is given by the Range Officer.
rules.reference: Small Arms Safety Manual & Range Standing Orders
rules.details: Muzzle awareness and chamber inspection drills must be executed without compromise.

rules.title: Mandatory Tactical Training & Drills
rules.explanation: Every soldier must regularly undergo Battle Physical Efficiency Tests (BPET), firing classification, and chemical-biological-radiological defense refreshers.
rules.reference: Annual Training Directives (Army Training Command - ARTRAC)
rules.details: Exemption from training is permitted only on certified medical advice from a Military Hospital Medical Officer.

rules.title: Hazard & Incident Reporting
rules.explanation: Personnel must immediately flag unsafe ammunition boxes, vehicle brake failures, exposed wiring, or combustible hazards to the Base Safety Officer.
rules.reference: Reference pending verification (Occupational Safety SOP)
rules.details: Unit safety officers conduct periodic risk assessments. Early reporting of near-misses prevents loss of life.

rules.title: Medical & Physical Fitness Compliance
rules.explanation: All servicemen must maintain prescribed physical conditioning and undergo mandatory annual medical examinations (AME) to ensure SHAPE-1 deployment readiness.
rules.reference: Medical Regulations for the Army
rules.details: Undisclosed injuries or refusal of medical treatment required for duty readiness is prohibited.

categories.title: Reporting Violations
categories.subtitle: Reporting misconduct through authorized channels and escalating safety concerns.
previewBullets: Reporting disciplinary infractions through authorized command channels
Immediate escalation of security breaches and perimeter hazards
Understanding statutory grievance redressal procedures without fear

rules.title: Reporting Misconduct through Official Channels
rules.explanation: Soldiers witnessing serious misconduct, theft of defence equipment, or insubordination must report the facts truthfully to their Subedar Major or Commanding Officer.
rules.reference: Army Rules, 1954 — Chapter IV (Investigation of charges)
rules.details: Anonymous or malicious false allegations are punishable under military law.

rules.title: Escalation of Urgent Security Breaches
rules.explanation: Intrusion alerts, perimeter fence breaches, or missing weapons must be reported instantaneously to the Base Duty Officer (BDO) and Guard Commander.
rules.reference: Base Counter-Sabotage & Alert Standard Operating Procedures
rules.details: The QRT is dispatched immediately upon broadcast of an alert code.

rules.title: Statutory Redress of Grievances
rules.explanation: Any serviceman who deems himself wronged by an officer has the statutory right under the Army Act to submit a petition for redress of grievance.
rules.reference: Army Act, 1950 — Section 26 & Section 27 (Redress of wrongs)
rules.details: Commanding Officers are legally mandated to investigate and forward petitions without bias or punitive retaliation.
